subject: ventures/photo-editing
professional: a working event/wedding photographer who also edits video (culls 2,000 frames after a shoot, grades with LUTs in Resolve/Lightroom, cuts social reels); first checks: is the copy off the card verified and non-destructive, does the cull keep the sharp-at-100% frame and not throw away deliberate low-key or high-key shots, is the LUT applied correctly, are the exports the right size and codec for Instagram

evidence.correctness: Ran it, not only read it. (a) Built a 4-file card (two JPEGs, an H.264 MP4, a ProRes MOV) with ffmpeg lavfi sources in the scratchpad and ran `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m shootflow.cli execute-ingest --confirm` then `run-local-pipeline --max-concurrency 3`: exit 0, 13.7 s, all stages complete. Recomputed independently: sha256sum of the four card files equals the sha256 of the four files under originals/ (set diff empty); ffprobe of outputs: reel and 3 variants h264 1080x1920 5.0 s, carousel and photo-set JPEGs 1080x1350, ProRes master prores 1280x720 2.0 s, proxy photo 1024x576, proxy video 960x540. (b) LUT: wrote a 2-point inverting .cube by hand, dropped it at color/shoot_look.cube, reran; one pixel of IMG_0002.JPG read via ffmpeg before 225,149,94 and after 29,106,161; 255-225=30, 255-149=106, 255-94=161, so within 1 level of the hand inversion. (c) Frame metrics against numpy (numpy 2.4.6) on synthetic frames: Laplacian variance 251.57232704 tool vs 251.57232704 numpy; luma mean/std/clipped-shadow/clipped-highlight identical to 8 digits on a random frame; Immerkaer noise on sigma-6 Gaussian frame: tool 5.93, textbook sqrt(pi/2)/6 mean-abs formula 6.03, true std 5.98; dHash of a ramp equals an independent 9x8 box-average implementation (0000000000000000); exposure for a flat 60 frame 0.5 vs hand 1-|60-120|/120 = 0.5; tilt on soft-edged horizons set at +1,+3,-4,+6 degrees read 0.98, 3.01, -4.09, 6.08 with the README's sign convention. A hard (unantialiased) 3 degree stair-step edge reads 0.0 degrees with confidence 0.93, a stated limit (soft edges only). (d) `shootflow.cli cull` on 5 ffmpeg-made photos: blurred copy flagged blurry (sharpness 0.062), near-black frame flagged blurry+bad exposure, a 0.02-darker duplicate beat the original (exposure 0.990 vs 0.932); I recomputed both exposures from a numpy decode of the 320x180 gray frame: 0.9319 and 0.9903. Xmp ratings written 4/2/-1/-1/4 as documented. All of this is synthetic media; no real camera file was available, so correctness stops at 3.
evidence.completeness: Claims checked in README against a run: checksummed non-destructive ingest (works), proxies (works), LUT grade for MP4/MOV/JPEG (works, verified above), reel + variant reels + carousel + photo set (6 render tasks all complete), idempotent reruns / launchd plist (write-launchd-plist not run; macOS-only, VideoToolbox path not exercisable on Linux), cull with --write-xmp (works), --picks and --thumbs (not run). Stated, honest gaps: RAW stills stop before grade, no RAW development, look and scene stages are stand-ins, all grading happens before selection. No TODO or NotImplementedError in src. The product is a CLI with no app; the 'Mac app' is direction only. Counted as 3: everything the README says works did, on the happy path.
evidence.verification: `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` ran 508 tests in 22 s: 1 failure, 1 skipped. The failure (test_workspace_health.test_unreadable_render_input_is_reported_for_review) is chmod(0) on a file, which does nothing when the audit runs as root (uid 0), so it is an environment artefact, not a product bug, but the suite is not green as run. Seeded mutation 1: in frame_analysis.py exposure target changed from 120 to 100 (`abs(mean - 100.0) / 120.0`): the whole suite (508 tests) still only had that one root failure, i.e. NOT caught, because the exposure test only checks extremes (dark and blown give 0.0, good > 0.6). Mutation 2: story_score tilt penalty zeroed (`crooked = 0.0`): tests test_frame_analysis, test_cull, test_story, test_ffmpeg_pipeline (63 tests) all passed, NOT caught, because test_crooked_horizon_loses_story_score passes on other metrics that differ between the two frames. Both reverted with git checkout; git status clean. Good points: tests include real-ffmpeg cases and noise recovered within 20%; the numeric core of the scoring is under-pinned though.
evidence.craft: Read frame_analysis.py in full, sampled cull.py, ingest.py (sha256 verify of copy and temp file then rename, manifest written via temp file: good), ffmpeg_media.py headers. 23,267 lines of stdlib Python in src/shootflow, with production_adapter.py 3,167 lines and cli.py 2,346 lines. A large parallel dry-run stack (render_adapter, render_scheduler, production_scheduler, render_workspace, workflow_authority) sits next to the real ffmpeg path, i.e. two engines. Per-pixel Python loops (framing, tilt, noise, Laplacian) at 320x180 are tolerable for stills but have no vectorised path, and every asset is graded before selection (README admits it). `ruff check src tests` reports 68 errors (31 unsorted imports, 11 blind-except BLE001, 11 SIM117), mypy not installed here so not run. Constants (half point 60, grey target 120, 0.85/0.15 weights) are unexplained magic numbers without a calibration set. No silent fallback found in the stages run; a failed job is marked retryable and the CLI exits 2 as documented.
evidence.claims: README is detailed and states its limits well (synthetic only, not tested on real camera files, RAW not developed, framing locates detail not subject). llms.txt is accurate and consistent with the run. BUT the published product page ventures/photo-editing/site/index.html (the only public marketing surface) says twice 'The renderers are dry-run placeholders: ShootFlow does not yet render video or grade images' (FAQ 'Does it render video or grade images yet? No.'), which my run falsifies: the pipeline produces graded ProRes/H.264 masters and 1080x1920 reels. The same page tells users to run `shootflow cull FOLDER --out REPORT`, but there is no `shootflow` executable (pyproject.toml says deliberately not packaged; `which shootflow` empty; the working form is `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m shootflow.cli cull`). The page does carry the disclaimer and a no-analytics statement. I could not load https://marisstella.app/photo-editing/ (proxy returned 000), so this read is of the source file that is deployed. The error understates the product, but a user reading it would not try the main feature, and the copy-paste command fails.
evidence.fitness: Job: a photographer ingests a card, culls, grades, and gets reels/carousels. Walked through it on synthetic media: ingest and exports work in one command each, nothing is uploaded, and the nightly launchd job is a good fit for the job. Gaps in the first hour: no UI (CLI, PYTHONPATH incantation, no install), RAW stills (the common pro format) halt the pipeline at the grade stage, reels are silent, 4 s clips, with no music or beat sync, the look stage is a stand-in so grading is only whatever LUT the user supplies, ranking is technical not taste, and none of it has been run on a real shoot or compared with a human's picks (the page itself says so). VENTURE.yaml stage: prototype and the hypotheses are untested, so 2 is fair.
evidence.domain: Compared against how a working photographer culls (Photo Mechanic / Lightroom: focus checked at 100% on the eyes, blink and expression, keep one per burst) and standard LUT/colour practice. Departures: sharpness and exposure are read from a 320x180 area-downscaled gray frame, which hides the fine-scale focus miss that is the main reason a pro rejects a frame; exposure is mean luma against a fixed grey target of 120 with a 2x clipping penalty, which will penalise deliberate low-key, night or snow high-key shots; a flat frame is labelled 'blurry' (dark.jpg got reasons blurry + bad exposure) which is a misleading reason to show the user; eyes-open needs an external detector and is off by default; the LUT is applied with no colour-space handling beyond the file (the user must supply a matching log-to-709 LUT). Strengths: sha256-verified non-destructive ingest and checksummed manifests match good DIT practice, XMP sidecars follow Adobe star/label semantics (4/2/-1, Red), and the burst grouping by dHash with single linkage is a standard approach. A professional would use it for ingest and as a first-pass cull suggestion, not sign it off as a cull.

defects.what: The public product page tells users the renderers are dry-run placeholders and that ShootFlow does not render video or grade images, which is false (a real run produced graded ProRes/H.264 masters and 1080x1920 reels). It also says to run `shootflow cull`, a command that does not exist (the tool is not packaged).
Core scoring constants are not pinned by tests: shifting the exposure grey target from 120 to 100, or removing the tilt penalty from story_score, leaves all tests green.

Sharpness, exposure and tilt are measured on a 320x180 downscale, so critical-focus misses are invisible; mean-luma exposure penalises low-key and high-key frames; flat dark frames are labelled 'blurry'.
RAW stills stop the pipeline before the grade stage, so the most common professional input cannot go end to end.
test_unreadable_render_input_is_reported_for_review fails when the suite runs as root because chmod(0) does not block reads; it should skip when os.geteuid() == 0.
ruff reports 68 errors (31 unsorted imports, 11 blind excepts) and a parallel dry-run adapter/scheduler stack duplicates the real ffmpeg path (production_adapter.py 3,167 lines, cli.py 2,346 lines).
A hard, unantialiased tilted edge reads 0.0 degrees tilt at 0.93 confidence (stair-step gradients vote at 0 and 45 degrees); only soft edges are measured correctly.

verdict: ShootFlow does what its README says on synthetic media: I ran a four-file card through checksummed ingest and the full local pipeline and got verified copies, a LUT grade that matches a hand-computed inversion, correctly sized reels, carousels and ProRes masters, and I reproduced its frame metrics (Laplacian variance, luma statistics, exposure, noise, dHash, tilt) against numpy and textbook formulas. It does not meet the bar because claims and verification are below 3: the public page says it cannot render or grade (it can) and names a command that does not exist, and two deliberate mutations of core scoring logic (the exposure target and the tilt penalty) passed the 508-test suite. It is finished against its own README (completeness 3) but is a prototype for a working photographer: no real-shoot validation, RAW unsupported past scoring, a 320x180 analysis frame, and no UI.
